metas.name: City Roads, Cochabamba
metas.note: Cochabamba is situated in a large flat valley, where you will almost always see an imposing wall of mountains to your north. This is the single most useful and consistent way of distinguishing this city from other places in Bolivia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, Eastern La Paz
metas.note:
La Paz and El Alto are twin cities that together form one big metropolitan area. However, despite being located right next to each other, they each have a very different look.

In many parts of La Paz but primarily in the urban East and surrounding roads, you can see these heavily eroded, pillar-like rock formations on the hillsides. They consist of a very recognizable yellow-beige sandstone (see image). Landslides seem to be common.

Of the big cities with coverage in Bolivia, these rock formations are essentially unique to La Paz.

The further out you go from the city, the more it turns to rolling green hills and patchy high altitude farmland.

Further East still and you begin to see the snow capped peaks of Layqa Qullu and Illimani.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, El Alto
metas.note:
El Alto is situated on a very flat, highland plateau. It looks much drier and dustier than La Paz. The layout of its streets is also more regular and grid-like.

The city appears like an unending mess of semi-finished red brick buildings, even more so than other cities in Bolivia. Some neighbourhoods have a very rundown, desolate look.

Pavement consisting of rectangular grey bricks with slightly wavy edges is very common in El Alto (see image).

You can sometimes see a local type of architecture referred to as Neo-Andean. Buildings in this style are colourful, with elaborate, futuristic-looking façades. The style is really unique and is almost completely limited to El Alto (see image).

Gates and doors are sometimes painted with a gradient pattern, usually dark green to light green, or red to yellow (see image).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, La Paz Central
metas.note:
La Paz and El Alto are twin cities that together form one big metropolitan area. However, despite being located right next to each other, they each have a very different look.

La Paz is a very hilly city. Most of La Paz itself is situated in meandering valleys, surrounded by hills that often tend to be covered in green vegetation as opposed to the more dry hillsides found in many other Bolivian urban areas (see image).

Downtown La Paz is the only place in Bolivia where you will find very tall buildings of 10+ storeys (see image).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, Oruro
metas.note:
Of all the major cities in Bolivia, Oruro is situated in by far the most dry landscape.

In Oruro, you will also usually be able to see a large dry hill to your west, in an otherwise mostly flat and very arid landscape.

NOTE: Potosí is also located in an arid landscape. However, it is considerably hillier.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, Potosi
metas.note:
Potosí is also situated in a very hilly landscape, like Sucre. However, its landscape is much more arid, with little to no trees atop the hills.

In many parts of Potosí, to the South you can see this colossal pyramid-shaped mountain called Cerro Rico. It is famous for having massive quantities of silver ore, and as a result its surface is stripped bare by extensive mining – which is distinctly visible in the street view coverage (see image).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, Santa Cruz & Suburbs
metas.note:
Santa Cruz is the only large Bolivian city located in a tropical (and flat) landscape.

Note that there are several smaller towns around Santa Cruz that look essentially identical. Some of these have extensive side-road coverage too.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: City Roads, Sucre
metas.note:
Sucre is situated in a very hilly landscape, and as a result you can see many elevation changes in its streets. Uniquely, you can see these round, tree-covered hills in many parts of the city.

It has a well-preserved historic city centre, with lots of old colonial buildings. The downtown area can be recognized by the white walls, orange tiled roofs, and generally more historic look than other places in Bolivia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, From Sillani
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Sucre, the most eastern of the three starts at Sillani and heads roughly South from there.

The sun is always visible to the NNW, and you will often see a drainage canal running alongside the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, North of Sacaba
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

North of Sacaba to the North East of Cochabamba lies a short unnamed section of cobbled road winding through the mountains with the city visible south.

The sun is always visible to the NW.

If you see Eucalyptus on a cobbled road, you are likely in the sections around Cochabamba rather than those around Sucre.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, Ruta 23, Section SE of Cochabamba
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Cochabamba lies a cobbled section of Ruta 23, heading in a NW/SE direction through grassy hills.

The Western part features clear skies with the sun in the NE and patchy tree coverage.

The Eastern part is mainly overcast, and has more vegitation, thickening out to forested hills as you travel East.

If you see Eucalyptus on a cobbled road, you are likely in the sections around Cochabamba rather than those around Sucre.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, Tarabuco To ICLA
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Sucre, the most Western of the three starts at Tarabuco and heads predominantly South East to ICLA.

The sun is always visible between N and NNE, and you will usually see a drainage canal running alongside the road.\
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, Through Cliza
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Cochabamba lies a short section of cobbled road passing through Cliza in a NW/SE direction.

In the Western stretch, some of the cobble is partially paved over with bits showing through, and sometimes Cochabamba's north imposing wall of mountains is visible.

The Eastern stretch features a low sun angle.

The sun direction ranges from N to NW.

If you see Eucalyptus on a cobbled road, you are likely in the sections around Cochabamba rather than those around Sucre.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, Through Tarabuquillo
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Sucre, the middle the three snakes roughly N/S passing through Tarabuquillo.

The sun is always visible to the NW, and you will sometimes see a drainage canal running alongside the road.\
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, Through Tin Tin
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Cochabamba lies a short section of cobbled road passing through Tin Tin in a NE/SW direction.

You should be able to make out a dark smudge glitch when facing forward, and you will often be able to see a small stream to the West of the road.

The sun is always visible to the NW, and this section has some sunset coverage.

If you see Eucalyptus on a cobbled road, you are likely in the sections around Cochabamba rather than those around Sucre.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Cobbled Road, Totora To Aiquile
metas.note:
Though fairly common in cities (especially Cochabamba), there are only a handful of rural cobbled roads, and they can be differentiated with some practice. Five exist to the East of Cochabamba, and three to the East of Sucre. Ruta 23 is the only main road with coverage of a cobbled section.

South East of Cochabamba, lies a long section of cobbled road snaking through mountains from Totora To Aiquile in a N/S direction. This is the furthest East of the Cochabamba adjacent cobbled roads.

There is sometimes a blur glitch visible when facing forward.

The sun is always visible between N and NNW.

The Southern part of this road in particular features large cacti including Cereus Stenogonus and Harrisia Trtracantha.

If you see Eucalyptus on a cobbled road, you are likely in the sections around Cochabamba rather than those around Sucre.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: La Paz To Huayna Potosi Mountain
metas.note:
This rocky mountain road heads North out of La Paz up towards the Huayna Potosi Mountain through grassy rolling hills.

The city is visible South in the lower section, and the mountain visible North in the upper section.

A river & several lakes are visible to the West of the road in many locations, as well as irrigation channels, often with running water.

The sky is mostly overcast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: N Yungas Road (AKA Death Road)
metas.note:
The N Yungas Road (also popularly known as Death Road), is a small, bendy and unpaved road, high up in the mountains east of La Paz with very tropical vegetation.

The coverage in the southern part of the road is very foggy. True to its unofficial name, this road looks like a very dangerous drive.

You can sometimes see some daring cyclists.

NOTE: The northern half of this road looks less foggy and dangerous. However, it should still be recognizable, as it is the only dirt road meandering through jungle hills in Bolivia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Roads near Death Road
metas.note:
Paved roads which vibe like a combination of the Pongo section and Death Road but higher in the mountains.

Clouds and fog, sometimes fogging up the camera.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 1 & 4, La Paz to Oruro
metas.note:
Ruta 1 and 4 between La Paz and Oruro is a large divided highway that runs through the Altiplano landscape of western Bolivia.

It is the only large, divided highway in the entire country. There are smaller, divided roads in and near some urban areas, but those should be easily distinguishable based on landscape and road size.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 1, Challapata To Guindal
metas.note:
Ruta 1 between Machacamarca and Guindal runs through an arid landscape where you will often see patches of snow on the hilltops, and sometimes even next to the road. Weather conditions range from cloudy to fully overcast, lending this coverage a gloomy look.

This section southeast of Challapata tends to be more curvy and hilly. The weather is much worse, with grey skies.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 1, Machacamarca To Challapata
metas.note:
Ruta 1 between Machacamarca and Guindal runs through an arid landscape where you will often see patches of snow on the hilltops, and sometimes even next to the road. Weather conditions range from cloudy to fully overcast, lending this coverage a gloomy look.

This section north of Challapata runs in a general NNW direction, with straight roads in flat terrain, with hills on one or both sides. Weather conditions are a little bit better, with some of the sky visible, especially when looking south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 1, West of El Alto
metas.note:
Ruta 1 west of El Alto is a paved road that runs through green grasslands. The road itself is mostly flat, but you will usually see hills nearby. On the road, you will often see numbers marked in white paint.

Near the western end of the road, close to Desaguadero and the border with Peru, you will be able to see Lake Titicaca to your North.

NOTE: This road can look very similar to Ruta 2 northwest of El Alto. Road angles can help if you are not sure.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 12 & Unnamed Roads Around Corque
metas.note: Around Corque, this section of Ruta 12, and the unnamed road branching off it heading South, are predominantly paved tarmac (as opposed to cracked concrete), but run through similar terrain - mostly flat semi-arid desert shrubland and salt flat with some hills.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 12 & Unnamed Roads Around Sabaya & Chipaya
metas.note:
Beginning at Huachacalla, this section of Ruta 12 is concrete, but not particularly cracked as more northern section are. Two unnamed and unpaved roads branch off it heading south to Sabaya and Chipaya respectively.

These roads all run through similar terrain - mostly flat semi-arid desert and salt flat beside several distinct hills which rise out of the plain.

The unpaved road to Chipaya has an overcast sky.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 12, Ancaravi To Hauchacella
metas.note:
Cracked concrete road heading NE/SW, through hilly semi-arid desert shrubland.

Overcast and dark in the southern section.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 12, Oruro to Toledo
metas.note:
A Cracked concrete road heading NE through semi-arid desert shrubland or salt flat with distant mountains.

Always has clear midday sky.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 19, El Alto To Viacha
metas.note:
Paved road heading NE/SW with snow capped mountains visible North and hills South through suburban grassland often with red dirt.

Weather is always overcast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 19, Viacha To Coro Coro
metas.note:
Paved road heading N/S through hilly grassland.

Weather is always overcast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 2 East & Various El Alto Plain Roads
metas.note:
South and West of El Alto, various roads weave through open grassland with some rolling hills. Salt deposits can be seen in places.

On Ruta 2 you can see the Andes in the distance.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 2, North of Titicaca
metas.note:
Lake Titicaca often visible to the West, South or both East and West, depending on where you are, with "Titicaca vibes" as you approach the lake.

The weather is mostly overcast to partially overcast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 23, Kuri To Aiquile Via Mizque
metas.note:
This section of Ruta 23 heads in a NW/SE direction and is paved (as opposed to cobbled).

Some of it, the stretch around Mizque, has the same dark smudge glitch when facing forward, as found in the Tin Tin cobble road coverage.

The sun is predominantly in the North, and the sky begins as overcast at Kuri, and progressively clearer skies the further East you are.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 25, Morochata
metas.note:
Around Morochata, northwest of Cochabamba on Ruta 25, there is a small isolated piece of coverage that looks extremely similar to Peru. It is a dirt road that meanders through a mountainous landscape. Knowing this road can be extremely helpful for country streak purposes.

The western part of this road is located in a green mountain landscape, with fields on the mountain slopes and lots of eucalyptus trees around.

Towards the east, it transitions into a more arid high altitude landscape that still looks very similar to Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 3, Around Pongo
metas.note:
The section of Ruta 3 around Pongo, northeast of La Paz, can easily be recognised by the breathtaking views of enormous mountains, which are often surrounded by low-hanging clouds.

The mountains are also recognizable by their dark grey rocks lightly covered in greenish grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 31, Oruro To Panduro
metas.note:
Paved and unpaved road running NW from Oruro to Panduro through salt flat and sandy, dusty plains with tufts of long grass in places.

The sky is mostly overcast and it feels stormy.

In the Eastern half heading mostly E/W, a fire can be seen burning to your South.

In the Western half heading mostly N/W, distant dust devils are sometimes visible to your SW.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 4, East of Santa Cruz
metas.note:
The section of Ruta 4 east of Santa Cruz, runs in a general east-west direction, through a mostly flat, green landscape.

In some places, you can see some low hills. This road has both asphalt and concrete pad sections.

Some sections feature Argentina-style Solid Yellow + Dashed White center lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 4, SW of Patacamaya, Grainy Road
metas.note: The section of Ruta 4, southwest of Patacamaya, runs through a semi-arid grassland landscape. Many parts of that road between Patacamaya and Callapa have worn-down grainy asphalt.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 4, SW, Nevado Sajama Views
metas.note:
On the southwesternmost section of Ruta 4, you can usually see the Nevado Sajama, an isolated snow-capped volcano that is very distinct and unlike any other mountain in Bolivia.

When you see Sajama, you will always be south of Callapa and the Desaguadero River. However, you will not always be able to see it on this section of the road, as it is often hidden by hills.

The southern section of this road sometimes features solid yellow + striped white roadlines as are found normally in Arg\Uruguay!

NOTE: The only other place where you can see Nevado Sajama is coverage in the National Park, which is recognizable by its unique Google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 4, Vila Vila to Buena Vista
metas.note:
This long section of Ruta 4 has a distinctive square smudge on the front left of the camera.

The affected coverage starts in the altiplano near Vila Vila, going east through Cochabamba, all the way to Buena Vista in the flat Amazonian part of Bolivia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 41 & Unnamed Roads, North of La Paz
metas.note: North of La Paz, Ruta 41 and several unnamed roads, all unpaved, snake through the mountain valleys with grass covered slopes reminiscent of the Scottish Highlands.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 5, Chaco, Sunset Coverage
metas.note:
The section of Ruta 5 around Chaco, just north of Sucre, has distinct sunset coverage. Most of this road has concrete pavement, and meanders through semi-arid hills.

Along these Northern sections of Ruta 5 the cacti 'Harrisia tetracantha' is quite common, terminating just South of Sucre and it can also be found along Ruta 7, and within Cochamabma.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 5, Potosi To Agua Castilla
metas.note:
This section of Ruta 5 is paved road heading NE/SW though hilly semi-arid desert shrubland and salt flat, with very dry sometimes tufty grass.

It has a similar feel to other roads running though the Southern desert plains such as Ruta 1 and 12, but it differs by being paved and always having clear sky.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 5, Sucre To Aiquile
metas.note:
These sections of Ruta 5 to the north of Sucre, above and below the Chaco sunset coverage, look fairly similar but they are paved or unpaved as opposed to concrete and the sun angle is low in the sky instead of full sunset and shines from a NW heading.

The road winds through rocky mountain valleys with dry but heavy shrub and tree coverage.

Along these Northern sections of Ruta 5 the cacti 'Harrisia tetracantha' is quite common, terminating just South of Sucre and it can also be found along Ruta 7, and within Cochamabma.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 5, Sucre To Potosi
metas.note:
This section of Ruta 5 runs South of Sucre to Potosi and has less plant coverage than more nortnern sections.\
The road winds in an arc through rocky mountain valleys with dry shrub coverage and sporadic trees.

The cacti 'Harrisia tetracantha' is common in the stretch just outside of Sucre, and can also be found on the Northern sections of Ruta 5, along Ruta 7, and within Cochamabma.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 6, Sora Sora To Pocoata
metas.note: Sun low in the sky, blur glitch very common (simlar but distinct from the R4, VilaVila To BuenaVista coverage)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 6, Sucre To Macha
metas.note:
This section of Ruta 6 is unpaved in the Western half, and winds through dry rocky hills with sporadic tree and bush cover, with density increasing the closer you get to Sucre.

The ground has significant grass coverage but it is a very dry light green colour, and straw coloured in places.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 6, Tarabuco To Zudanez
metas.note: The section of Ruta 6 between Tarabuco and Zudáñez is paved with extremely light-coloured concrete, bordering on white. This pavement is very recognizable and unique to this road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 7 & 22, Mataral Area
metas.note:
The roads around the town of Mataral have recognizable coverage: a very green, hilly landscape, and sunny weather with only a couple of clouds. While the hills are very green, the vegetation is not quite as dense as Santa Cruz area.

This coverage is limited to Ruta 7 from Comarapa to Mairana, and Ruta 22 to Vallegrande. Other roads in Bolivia with similar vegetation tend to either have different weather (overcast) or terrain (more flat).

You will often see large examples of cacti including Cereus Stenogonus and Harrisia Trtracantha hiding between the bushes, as well as trees with yellow flowers (potentially 'Pride of Bolivia' or perhaps more likely a species of Senna).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 7 & Unnamed Road, Totora To Tiraque
metas.note:
This section of Ruta 7 to the East of Cochabamba runs though hilly farmland with dry, sometimes tufty grass, and sparse but significant tree coverage. The streetview coverage branches off at Epizana to an unnamed road with a largely similar feel.

The Ruta 7 part has a significant amount of Eucalyptus planted along side it. Eucalyptus is common within Bolivian cities, but less so in such numbers on rural roads, though other rural roads in the SW of Cochabamba vicinty do have some, as well as Titicaca the area.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 7, Mairana To San Luis
metas.note:
The section of Ruta 7 between Mairana and the outskirts of Santa Cruz has coverage with a camera bug that causes a visual glitch. It is a distinctive, neon-like discoloration, that (depending on the road angle) is usually more or less to your north.

NOTE: This glitch can also rarely be found in some limited areas in and around Santa Cruz. In these areas, the glitch is often not as severe.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Ruta 9, Middle section
metas.note:
Paved usually straight road running majority N/S, cutting through the forest in the south and forest plains closer to Santa Cruz.

Sun directly overhead and mostly cumulus clouds or overcast.

Always travelling South.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Ruta 9, South section
metas.note:
Paved usually straight road cutting through the forest, running majority N/S along parallel moutain ridges.

Red soil is common & quite a few bollards can be seen along this stretch.

Sun gets lower in the sky the further North you travel.

Predominantly cirrus clouds in the sky.

Always travelling North.

North of Carini there are 2/3 smudges in front of the car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Sajama National Park Road
metas.note:
Sajama National Park was covered by this unique Google car: it has a black roof rack with a series of metal bars.

The coverage is on an unpaved road surrounded by fluffy bushes. The Nevado Sajama volcano is always visible. The car briefly drove through the small village of Tomarapi, which can be recognized by its traditional buildings with adobe walls and thatched roofs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Santa Cruz Plain Roads
metas.note:
The area east of the Andes is very green and tropical, with lots of agriculture – especially around Santa Cruz. This area is mostly very flat, though you will see large hills when closer to the Andes. The soil tends to have a red\pink colour and is often sandy.

Within the tropical areas of Bolivia, coverage on unpaved roads is only found around Santa Cruz.

There is some Trecker coverage on some sand dunes South of the city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Villa Catalina To Coipasa, Salt Flats
metas.note:
Between the villages of Villa Catalina and Coipasa, there is an isolated stretch of coverage where the Google car drove through extremely arid desert terrain. This small road is located close to the southwestern end of Ruta 12, near the Chilean border. It can be hard to spot on the map, because it blends in with the salt flat.

Closer to Villa Catalina, the car drove over the salt flat and near Coipasa, the car drove on an unpaved dirt road, where you can see cone-shaped volcanic hills. In both parts, there is virtually no vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.
